claims.proposition_evaluated: By 2026-09-23, Edmonton had removed motor-vehicle through lanes for built on-street bike lanes in at least 8 of its 15 district-plan areas.
claims.interpretation_notes: My round-1 verdict remains Not established. City records verify conversions in Central, Scona and North Central: a verified minimum A of 3. That is below both the primary threshold of 8 and alternative threshold of 5. I can identify at least five qualifying corridors or converted corridor segments, but I cannot calculate the built-corridor total T or complete the prior-use census R from the accessible inventory and project records. The same three district areas are represented when the verified segments are considered as individual inventory features; I cannot give a defensible feature-level C without filtering their geometry. The classification remains Not established in that unit and under the alternative threshold. A corridor's lane removal says nothing about whether congestion rose or fell. I do not count 132 Avenue from its draft design or projected construction, or 102 Avenue east of 109 Street from the LRT-related lane reduction.

limitations: The brief reports 3,175 features in its September 23, 2026 immutable snapshot. I could not independently retrieve and count that file in this round, so 3,175 is the supplied snapshot count, not a new calculation.
T and R at corridor level remain uncalculated. The consulted GIS layer has no prior-use field, and the project-record search is incomplete. The verified A of 3 is a minimum, not an upper bound.

The five identified qualifying segments do not constitute an exhaustive corridor list. The assessment of 83 Avenue and Garneau's 110 Street combines design documents with later evidence of route or project completion rather than block-level as-built drawings.

For 132 Avenue, the February 2022 report is a draft and the September 2026 update shows incomplete construction. The report identifies traffic calming and collector renewal as project purposes; it cannot establish that bike paths occupied former through-lane space on a completed segment.

For 102 Avenue between 121 and 111 Street, the City explicitly says it removed the westbound lane to fit the protected bike lane while retaining south-side parking. For the other qualifying segments, the City describes active transportation or neighbourhood renewal; those stated purposes do not resolve the parked counterfactual claim about why work would have proceeded without bike lanes.
I found no City-published length or network share of bike lanes occupying former through lanes.
unknowns: The complete built on-street bike-lane corridor set T, the documented-prior-use count R and any additional qualifying districts.
Feature-level C after the verified segments are intersected with the frozen inventory geometry.
Whether a City as-built drawing establishes a qualifying completed on-street conversion on any part of 132 Avenue by September 23, 2026.
Whether 102 Avenue east of 109 Street ever met the brief's specific through-lane-to-bike-lane test before the November 2025 temporary relocation.
Whether the separate 80 Avenue Garneau conversion placed its bike lane in former through-lane space, former parking space, or both.

what_would_change_my_verdict: City records verifying qualifying built corridors in at least eight district-plan areas would change the primary verdict to Supported.
A complete census with at least one qualifying corridor but fewer than eight represented areas would change the primary verdict to Partially supported.
claims.suggested_one_line: City records verify through-lane conversions for bike lanes in at least three Edmonton districts, but the available corridor census cannot establish whether they extend across a broad share of the city.
claims.suggested_short_answer: Not established. City records document built conversions on 102 Avenue, 96 Street, part of 100 Street, and streets in Garneau and Strathcona. They verify a minimum of three of Edmonton's 15 district-plan areas. The on-street bike-route inventory does not record prior lane use, and the corridor-by-corridor check is incomplete, so that minimum cannot decide whether removals occurred in eight districts. These findings do not measure any change in congestion.
